metadata.defaultTitle: ATS readability — see your CV the way the parser does
metadata.description: Read a CV the way an applicant tracking system reads it: what parses, what is missing, and which terms from the job ad never appear. Runs entirely in the browser.
metadata.openGraphDescription: See your CV the way the parser does. Nothing is uploaded.

common.disclaimer: The checks are heuristics built from how mainstream parsers behave, not a reproduction of any named vendor. A good score means nothing is standing between your CV and a human reader; it is not a prediction that you will be invited.

home.headline: Your CV is read as text, not as a design.
home.lede: An applicant tracking system throws away your layout and keeps whatever text it can pull out. This shows you that text, scores what survived out of 100, and lists what to change — ordered by how many points each fix is worth.
home.privacyNote: The file is read in your browser and scored there. It is never uploaded.
home.methodIntro: Each dimension starts at its full weight and loses points only to a named finding, so the report can always tell you where a missing point went.
home.methodNoBlackBox: Nothing here is a black box: every deduction names the line it came from and what to write instead.

parseability.name: Parseability
parseability.what: Whether the text layer survives extraction at all: columns, tables, icon fonts, broken encodings.

keywords.name: Keyword match
keywords.what: Coverage of the terms mined from the job ad, weighted by how central each one is to the posting.

impact.name: Impact
impact.what: Quantified results and ownership verbs, measured against responsibility filler.

structure.name: Structure
structure.what: Headings a parser can map to fields, dated entries in reverse order, bullets instead of paragraphs.

contact.name: Contact
contact.what: The identity fields every system stores: name, email, phone, location, profile link.

analyze.heading: See what the parser gets
analyze.lede: Upload the exact file you send to employers. The text below is what an applicant tracking system would extract — correct it if the extraction went wrong, then score it against the ad.

editor.title: Build a CV
editor.lede: Every field an applicant tracking system can store. Nothing is filled in for you, and a field you clear is removed rather than left empty.
editor.saveFailed: This browser refused local storage, so the draft is not kept. Download it before you leave.

editor.importSummary: Imported {name}: {review} fields need your review, {missing} could not be extracted and stayed empty.
editor.needsReview: Check this — the importer is not certain.
editor.confirmClear: Clear every field? This cannot be undone.

rewriteDiff.heading: Rewrite weak bullets
rewriteDiff.lede: The local model restates {count, plural, one {# responsibility bullet} other {# responsibility bullets}} as claims. Invented facts are filtered out before you see them; everything unknown stays a visible [quantify: …].
rewriteDiff.nothingUsable: The model returned nothing usable. The deterministic drafts below still work.
rewriteDiff.stale: The text changed since this proposal was made; regenerate the proposals.

entriesTable.heading: Entries as the parser separated them
entriesTable.lede: Each dated entry the parser could pull apart, and which sections it recognised at all.
entriesTable.noEntries: No dated entry could be separated. A parser that cannot find a date range cannot build an employment history from the document.
entriesTable.unusable: The end of this range precedes its start, so a parser cannot use it at all.

identityTable.heading: What the parser read as your details
identityTable.lede: The identity fields every applicant tracking system stores. Each one is shown as the parser extracted it.
identityTable.showLine: Show this line in the parsed text

reason.not-located: The checks count this as present, but no clean value could be lifted out of the text.
reason.split-across-lines: This only reads correctly once two lines are joined, so a parser sees two fragments and uses neither.
reason.buried-in-a-run: The value sits inside a long unbroken line, where a parser can run it together with its neighbours.
reason.nothing-resembling: Nothing in the document resembles this field.
reason.rejected-candidate: Something close is in the document, but a parser would not accept it: {candidate}

aiStatus.detecting: Checking what this machine can run locally…
aiStatus.heading: Text model
aiStatus.lede: Rewriting and explanations need a text model. Every option runs on your machine; none of them sees your CV until you ask for one of them.
aiStatus.ollamaUnreachable: Ollama did not answer on localhost:11434. Start it, and set OLLAMA_ORIGINS to include this site.

ollamaSetup.heading: Localhost connection
ollamaSetup.intro: The browser blocks access to your local machine for security. You must start Ollama with CORS configured so it accepts requests from this site.

byokSetup.heading: Bring Your Own Key
byokSetup.intro: Enter your API key and endpoint. Keys are stored locally in your browser and never sent to our servers. Every time a feature requests to send data, you will be prompted for consent.
byokSetup.consentHeading: Send CV data to external provider?
byokSetup.consentIntro: This feature requires sending your CV data to an external provider to process it. Your text will be sent to:
byokSetup.consentWarning: Review the provider's privacy policy before proceeding. Do not send sensitive data to providers you do not trust.

aiConsent.readyDetail: Hints below run locally against the parsed text; scores are unaffected.
aiConsent.heading: Semantic hints (optional)
aiConsent.lede: A small language model can point out near-misses the literal matcher cannot see - like a CV saying “Postgres” where the ad says “PostgreSQL”. It runs entirely in your browser ({model}, about {sizeMb} MB, downloaded once and cached). Your CV text is never sent anywhere, and scores never change - hints are advice, not measurement.
aiConsent.downloadFailed: The model could not be downloaded.

coverageMap.heading: What the CV never addresses
coverageMap.lede: The ad in {chunks, plural, one {# chunk} other {# chunks}}, each compared against the whole CV by the local model. These stay below {threshold}% similarity to anything you wrote. Advice, not measurement - the score is unchanged.
coverageMap.allCovered: Every part of the ad has a close counterpart in the CV.

findingExplain.error: The model could not answer - try again

fixDrafts.ledeBefore: Responsibility phrasing rewritten as a claim.
fixDrafts.ledeAfter: marks the part only you can fill in. Applying a draft re-runs the analysis so the score rail shows the difference.
fixDrafts.more: {count} more drafts appear as you resolve these.

documentIntake.pagesRead: {source} · {pages, plural, one {# page} other {# pages}} read
documentIntake.formats: PDF, DOCX or plain text, up to 10 MB. It is read in this browser and never sent anywhere.

sharedReport.lede: Scores and advice only. The CV itself was never stored.
sharedReport.cta: Run your own CV through it

coverLetter.heading: Cover letter
coverLetter.lede: A draft built from your CV and this ad. It may restate what your CV says and name the employer the ad names. Nothing else.
coverLetter.needsModel: Turn on a model to draft a letter. Everything runs in your browser.
coverLetter.failed: The model did not return a usable letter.
coverLetter.dropped: {count, plural, one {# paragraph went beyond what your CV says and was dropped} other {# paragraphs went beyond what your CV says and were dropped}}.
coverLetter.nothingSurvived: Every paragraph went beyond what your CV says, so none is shown. Add the evidence to your CV first, then draft again.

tailor.heading: Terms this ad asks for
tailor.lede: Each card quotes the line of the ad that asks for the term. Nothing enters your CV until you say you have the skill.
tailor.empty: This ad names no term your CV is missing.
tailor.confirmHint: Confirm first, then the term can be added.
tailor.writeItYourself: This one is a claim about work you did, so write it where you did it. The tool will not put words in your mouth.
tailor.alreadyThere: Your CV already names this term.
tailor.noSkillsSection: This CV has no skills section to add to. Add the heading first, or write the term where it belongs.

kanban.heading: Applications
kanban.lede: Track your applications. Data stays on your device.

interview.heading: Interview preparation
interview.lede: Story cards built from your CV, questions mapped to them, and a practice mode. Everything here works without a model; the ad-specific questions need one.
interview.storyBankLede: Each card is a verbatim slice of your CV. A slot the document does not fill is marked missing, never invented.
interview.storyBankEmpty: No achievement bullets found. Add quantified outcomes to your CV to build story cards.
interview.skippedHeading: {count, plural, one {# bullet skipped} other {# bullets skipped}}
interview.templateLede: Mapped to your story cards by topic overlap. A question your CV cannot answer keeps an empty list rather than borrowing a story that does not fit.
interview.noMatchingCard: No card in your CV covers this question.
interview.adLede: Questions generated from the terms in the job ad. Each one cites the term it targets. Requires a model.
interview.adNeedsModel: Turn on a model to generate questions from the ad. Everything runs in your browser.
interview.adFailed: The model did not return usable questions.
interview.adEmpty: The model produced no question that could cite a term from the ad.
interview.practiceLede: Pick a question above, type your answer, and the best matching story card is suggested. The match is traced to the words you typed.
interview.practicePlaceholder: Type how you would answer the question...
interview.practiceNoMatch: No card shares enough words with your answer to recommend one.
interview.practiceOverlap: {count, plural, one {# shared word} other {# shared words}}
